lines.text: Brother William calls it the gods' judgement.

lines.text: Brother William says a great deal lately. None of it kind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the lair burst and a thousand Horrors walked out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Five. Five is plenty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every leak feeds the waking. My grandfather swore it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Your grandfather swore the beacons kept the rain off.

who: townsfolk, refugees, guards and guild members

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Blight-born overran {hamlet}. Its people fled here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then that's a hamlet's food gone till the guild clears it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eight came through the gate from {hamlet}. Grey as ash.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give them bread. Don't ask what they saw.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {town} wants {hamlet} cleared, and fast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fast costs. Ask about the coin first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the dead of {hamlet} walk the fields now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody died. They ran, which was sensible.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another desert hamlet lost to the Blight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Coin has hamlets to spare. We don't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {hamlet}'s goats will give grey milk now, you watch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If anyone's left to milk them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band}'s camp has broken up. The last of them scattered.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Scattered where? Into our woods?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band}'s finished. Some will come to us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Feed them if they bring a blade. Turn them off if they don't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One less camp on the road.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One less camp. Same number of men.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard {band} turned on each other and hanged their captain.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Heard they ran out of bread. Makes a worse song.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With {band} gone, we might sleep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Till summer. They always come back by summer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} rode out and killed a Blight pack before it reached the hamlets.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good work. Well paid, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The town paid two hundred and forty coin for that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cheaper than losing a hamlet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four Blight-born, six of us. Clean.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clean until the next four.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {guild} killed forty Blight-born in a night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Four. Ask them yourself. They'll tell you forty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The guild earns its coin this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: See {steward} notes it. And notes the price.

who: townsfolk, refugees, guild members and outlaws

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} took {hamlet} and stayed. Its people are in our streets.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And its fields feed outlaws now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A hundred and more from {hamlet}, sleeping on our doorsteps.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And eating from our granary, while {band} eats theirs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Contract's up to retake {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twenty-odd outlaws dug in behind farm walls. Not cheap, not easy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Deserters holding our land. Sir John should hang every one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: First he has to catch them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard the outlaws crowned a king at {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They crown a new king every week out there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} holds {hamlet}. Fields, roofs, a well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Feels like being a lord. Till the guild comes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Beds are full. Refugees are camped by the walls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And eating from the granary. Ours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We should open the temple to them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We have. They're sleeping on the altar steps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We can't feed ourselves, never mind a camp of strangers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Say it louder. Let them hear what we've become.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thousands by the walls, I heard. A city of tents.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A hundred and sixty. Enough to make a hamlet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The camp by the walls is restless tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hungry folk are restless. Keep your torch lit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Refugees by the walls, and the granary's full.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then let them eat. Kindness is cheap this season.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Beaten twice by the Blight, {band} has moved camp.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Closer to us, or further?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Packed up and walked two hours. Lost a cart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lost less than staying would've cost.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} moved. We'll need new patrol routes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} will say there's no oil for new routes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} ran clean out of the hold, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three miles. They ran three miles.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band}'s new fire is nearer the road now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we take the long way to market.

who: townsfolk, refugees, guild members and clergy

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} cleared {hamlet} of Blight-born. Settlers are going back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Somebody has to plant.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We're going home to {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check the well before you drink from it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three hundred and sixty coin for clearing {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Split nine ways. Less the healer's bill.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {guild} burned {hamlet} to clear it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They cleared the Blight-born. The burning was the Blight's.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone should bless {hamlet} before they settle.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Brother William offered.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: Then perhaps someone else.

who: townsfolk, returning hamlet folk and outlaws

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {hamlet}'s retaken. {band} driven out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Its people can go home, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Back in {hamlet}. The outlaws mended my roof.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't say that too loud round here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One family in {hamlet} fed {band} the whole time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they'll need friends now. They won't find any.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} lost {hamlet}. Eight guild swords did it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eight good ones. We'd have needed thirty to hold.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the guild hanged every outlaw at {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Most ran. Outlaws are good at running.

who: craftsfolk, townsfolk and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Notice on the gate. {town} wants a journeyman smith.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lost ours, then. To what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No weaponsmith in {town}. Who mends the guards' blades?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody. They'll be swinging sticks by spring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're begging for a smith over there. Good coin offered.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tempting. Their ale's dreadful, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the last smith was murdered over a debt.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He went where the wages are better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A town without a weaponsmith is a town without a garrison.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} knows. He wrote the notice himself.

who: craftsfolk, townsfolk and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {town} hired a journeyman away from another hold. A hundred and fifty coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's poaching, that is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They lured our best smith off with coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then pay better and keep the next one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New smith starts tomorrow. Mind your manners.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll mind my tools. New smiths borrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard the new smith cost a thousand coin and a house.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hundred and fifty. The house is a loft over the tannery.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buying craftsmen from rival holds. {lord} plays a long game.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every game's long when nobody's king.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Seven from {hamlet} came home from the slavers' holds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ransomed. Who paid?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ring the bell for {hamlet}'s folk.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Count them first. Make sure it's all of them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Seven taken from {hamlet}. Six came back, I heard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hush. The mother's in the next room.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stonepass paid the ransom again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Paying slavers teaches slavers the way back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One of the {hamlet} girls speaks their tongue now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then she knows what they said about us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} hit the carts from {hamlet}. The grain's gone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Escort couldn't hold?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Six against fourteen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We lost the carts. Two of ours dead on the road.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't tell their wives here. Wait till morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That grain was our bread. Now {band} eats it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then go and ask {band} for supper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The escort sold the route, they're saying in {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Escorts die on that route. Mostly they don't sell it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {band} took a hundred carts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {hamlet} doesn't own a hundred carts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Somebody pays {band} to choose which carts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Somebody with Sunward silver, I'd wager.

who: townsfolk, guild members, clergy and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One of ours came home from the tower school. A trained mage.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And went back to the old trade, they say. Strange choice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A trained mage, and nobody's signed them yet?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Get to them before {guild} does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Magic in a cobbler's shop. What next?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Next it's in your shop. The leylines don't ask permission.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Heard they came back able to call fire from the sky.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They came back able to light a hearth without flint.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A mage in town owes nothing to {lord}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then {lord} will make them owe him. One way or another.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {hamlet}'s abandoned. Struck three times in three weeks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nobody stays for a fourth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Seven walked in from {hamlet} today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Walked. With nothing but what was on their backs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every time {hamlet} empties, someone buys it cheap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone who can afford to wait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Another desert hamlet left to the sand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Coin will just buy new farmers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {hamlet}'s cursed. Food left on the tables.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Food left because they ran. That's no curse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Folk going out to resettle {hamlet}. Safe a fortnight, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A fortnight isn't safe. It's quiet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We'll have {hamlet}'s fields sown by autumn.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If nothing comes through first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The settlers found the old larders still full at {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then nobody ate there. Ask yourself why.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A season before {hamlet} feeds us again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then a lean season. Tighten your belt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {lord}'s giving land at {hamlet} to anyone who'll take it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Giving it to six fools with spades.

who: everyone: townsfolk, clergy, guild members, wardens and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A calamity's risen in the March. They're calling it {calamity}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They name them now? Like lords?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {calamity}. Say the name and the wells sour, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Superstition. But don't say it in here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {calamity} ate a whole fort, garrison and all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It rose in a broken fort. Nobody's garrisoned those in twenty years.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} will want a party for {calamity}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {guild} will want ten parties. And a priest for each.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ash-light over the March last night. Now we know its name.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {calamity}. Light the beacon early.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A named calamity. {lord} will want its head for his crown.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Kill a monster, claim a throne. Oldest story there is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Will {calamity} come here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything comes here in the end. Plant anyway.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Season's turning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wind's different. Smells of change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New season. Maybe a kinder one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Seasons don't care whether we eat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New season. The camps fill back up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twenty-five men by the turn. Same as every year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The rites change with the season. Fetch the right cloths.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which ones? I've lost track of the calendar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New season, new tithe.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {steward} has the rolls ready already.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: New season and the granary's full. Remember this one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'll carve it on a post.

who: townsfolk, guards, outlaws and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band}'s back at the old camp. Twenty-five men already.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Broken in spring, whole by summer. Like weeds.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Back at the old fire. Same stones, new faces.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some old faces too. The ones who ran fastest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} again. How many times must a hero break them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every season. That's the trade.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {band} has a hundred men now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twenty-five. But they boast like a hundred.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} has re-formed. Shall I send for the hero?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not yet. Let them grow. They're useful a while.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Blight's spreading. The dens grow every season.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like rot in a beam. Slow, then sudden.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The nest is bigger. I counted the glow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Count less. Sleep more. Counting won't stop it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The grey's reaching the near pastures.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then move the goats. Again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Blight grows and the faithful shrink.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The faithful were never many.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the Blight will reach {town} by winter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They said that last winter.

who: guild members, clergy, townsfolk and outlaws

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A {guild} party went into the rift. None came back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Five. All five.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {dead} was in that party.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {dead} always came back. That was the whole point of {dead}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Five names to read tonight. {dead} among them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Read them slowly. Nobody else will.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A whole guild went into the rift, I heard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A party. Five. A whole guild would be news.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} lost a party in the rift. Their gear's still down there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the queen's people will be first to it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {guild} will be recruiting by morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Five empty benches. They fill quicker than graves.

who: townsfolk, guild members, clergy, outlaws and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lords marched on the Heart of the Blight. Thinned it by half.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half. That's still half a Demon King.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} sent heroes with the expedition.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And will want the credit for all of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lords get the glory. {guild} gets the leftovers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leftovers pay. Glory gets you buried.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half the Heart broken. The gods be thanked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thank the soldiers first. Then the gods.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the lords killed the Demon King himself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If they had, you'd hear bells, not gossip.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With the heroes off at the Heart, the roads are ours.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For a week. Make it count.

who: everyone: townsfolk, clergy, guild members and the lord's household

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The cataclysm of the rift is slain. Dead for good.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nothing like it rises there again, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A cataclysm slain. I never thought I'd ring bells for that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ring them twice. Once for the dead who did it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whose blade was it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everyone claims it. Nobody shows the wound.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say the Blight's ending now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: One rift's gone quiet. The Heart still beats.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A cataclysm down. The holds will fight over the credit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the throne goes to whoever tells it best.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does a dead cataclysm mean cheaper bread?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It means one less thing to blame for dear bread.
